fields.description:
## Context

The calibration program lacks an empirical Tier-3 catch-power signal. Tests pass deterministic Tier-1/Tier-2 checks (assertion shape, intent articulation, manifest-claim breadth and header-source from 7f42) while sometimes failing to catch behavior-changing mutations on the code they claim to verify. Without mutation testing, the project has no empirical ground truth for "does this test catch a real regression?" — only structural proxies. The DSO maintainer, sprint orchestrators, and code-reviewer-test-quality have no visibility into per-PR kill-rate trends; the project cannot tell whether changes to test-writing prompts (d566, 69e8 graduations) are actually improving test catch-power.

This epic delivers per-PR mutation testing for the DSO plugin's first-class stacks (Python, Ruby, JS/TS, Flask, Go), runs in parallel with llm-review as a non-blocking CI job, ships calibration-first with a count-floor surfacing a maintainer-review story ticket, and after thresholds are committed enters enforcement mode where threshold breach auto-creates a bug ticket. Bash is out of scope due to the absence of mature mutation tooling in the bash ecosystem.

## Success Criteria

SC1: plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md published. Per-stack-result schema: {stack, mutation_tool, tool_version, total_mutants, mutants_generated (distinct field — zero indicates PR touched only non-mutable code), killed_mutants, surviving_mutants: [{file, line, operator, expected, actual}], kill_rate, runtime_seconds, runtime_exceeded (bool), exit_status}. Aggregate-result schema: {pr_number, schema_version=1, calibration_mode_active, per_stack_results: [...], aggregate_kill_rate}. Tooling MUST preserve unknown fields in passthrough for forward-compatibility.

SC2 (Phase 1 — Python pilot): plugins/dso/workflows/mutation-testing.yml shipped as plugin template. Triggered on pull_request (synchronize, opened). Concurrency group keyed to PR ref so new commits cancel in-flight runs. PR-label `skip-mutation-testing` opts a PR out entirely (cost-control escape hatch). When PR's mutable-stack file count exceeds `mutation.max_files_per_run` (default 100), workflow auto-skips with annotation suggesting label use or PR split. Python matrix job installs mutmut pinned to `mutation.python.tool_version` from dso-config.conf; on install failure, tries `mutation.python.fallback_versions` in order; final failure emits `TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED` annotation distinguishing tool-yank from mutation-failure. Runs mutmut incremental mode against diffed Python files. Writes findings JSON per SC1. Uploads as workflow artifact. Aggregate job upserts PR comment with marker `MUTATION_TESTING_FINDINGS_<pr-number>` (distinct from llm-review's marker — no race possible), writes GHA workflow summary, falls back to GHA-summary-only when comment-write is unavailable (fork PRs). Operates in calibration mode (no enforcement, no auto-bug-creation).

SC3 (Phase 2 — polyglot expansion): Ruby (mutant), JS/TS (Stryker `--incremental`), Go (go-gremlins) added as parallel matrix jobs alongside Python. Flask covered by Python. Each per-stack job installs its tool pinned to `mutation.<stack>.tool_version` with `mutation.<stack>.fallback_versions` chain. Per-stack runtime cap via `mutation.<stack>.timeout_seconds` (defaults: Stryker 600, mutmut 900, mutant 1200, gremlins 900). On timeout, partial-result emitted with `runtime_exceeded=true`. fail-fast: false across matrix entries. When ALL stacks return `runtime_exceeded=true`, PR comment surfaces prominent `ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT` warning, no bug ticket created (even in threshold mode), `aggregate_kill_rate=null`. Aggregate job merges all stack findings into a single PR comment.

SC4 (Phase 3 — calibration auto-surfacing): CI workflow tracks accumulated telemetry. Floor: ≥20 PRs telemetry AND ≥4 weeks elapsed since first telemetry run AND no existing `mutation-calibration-review` tagged story ticket — all three conditions required. Workflow auto-creates story ticket titled "Review mutation testing telemetry and set per-stack thresholds". Body opens with: "Your observed kill rate is X%. What threshold fits your project's risk tolerance?" (number not headlined). Reference points table with p25 / median / p75 rows and a second column "Approximate alert frequency" showing what share of PRs would fire a threshold alert at that rate. Self-reflection prompt: "Does your calibration window include PRs that modified test files? If most PRs in the window were non-test, this kill rate may underestimate steady-state." Stable tag `mutation-calibration-review` prevents duplicate creation. Workflow emits config-consistency warning annotation when `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate` is set but `mutation.calibration.completed=false` (or vice versa).

SC5 (Phase 4 — threshold-mode enforcement): Workflow reads `mutation.calibration.completed` from dso-config.conf. When true AND per-stack `mutants_generated > 0`: per-stack kill rate compared against `mutation.threshold.<stack>.min_kill_rate`. On breach, bug ticket auto-created via `.claude/scripts/dso ticket create bug` pushing to the tickets orphan branch using the same CI auth pattern as the existing Jira bridge / outbound checkpoint. Retry-with-backoff (3 attempts); on final failure writes `TICKET_CREATE_FAILED` artifact to the workflow run plus a workflow-level annotation. Bug ticket includes a 4-field structured blurb (max 60 words total):
- WHAT — one sentence on what mutation testing caught
- THRESHOLD — specific threshold that fired plus current kill rate
- CONTEXT — link to behavioral-testing-standard.md Tier-3 rationale and 411b epic for background
- NEXT_STEP — instructs investigating agent: investigate surviving mutants; do NOT adjust the threshold

Content-hash deduplication tag `mutation-breach-<sha>` where sha is hash(stack, source_file, mutant_locations) — scoped per-stack-per-source-file, NOT per-PR-diff. Recurring root-causes dedup correctly across PRs; structurally-similar diffs in different files don't collide.

SC6 (Phase 5 — onboarding integration): The consolidated `/dso:onboarding` (delivered by dependency 136b-6758) gains a mutation-testing phase. LEADS WITH TRADEOFFS before per-stack questioning: estimated CI time cost, false-positive context, and one sentence on what the maintainer is asked to do when bugs fire. Detects in-scope stacks via manifest files (Python: pyproject.toml or setup.py; Ruby: Gemfile; JS/TS: package.json; Go: go.mod). Single-stack auto-default: detected single in-scope stack auto-enables with a one-line notice "Mutation testing defaulted ON for <stack> — run /dso:onboarding --mutation-off to disable". Multi-stack: per-stack Socratic-confirm after the tradeoff context block. Writes `mutation.<stack>.enabled` keys to dso-config.conf. Copies `mutation-testing.yml` to `.github/workflows/`. Ensures the tickets-branch push permission scope exists in CI auth configuration. Documents bash as unsupported in the dialogue with ecosystem-limitation rationale.

SC7 (Phase 5 — create-dso-app.sh setup-script integration): plugins/dso/scripts/create-dso-app.sh updated. When scaffolding a new DSO-using project, the script applies the same single-stack-auto-default + multi-stack-confirm pattern as SC6. Writes default `mutation.<stack>.enabled=true` for detected stacks. Copies mutation-testing.yml alongside other CI workflow templates. Adds tickets-branch push permission to CI auth section. Coordination via ticket comment on d765-a3b6-84bd-4816 noting 411b's setup-script touchpoints.

SC8 (out-of-scope documentation + scope-seal): mutation-testing.yml header contains an explicit scope-seal block:

```
# SCOPE-SEALED: bash mutation tooling is out of scope — see 411b epic; do not reopen.
# Rationale: no mature mutation testing tool exists in the bash ecosystem.
# Supported stacks: Python (mutmut), Ruby (mutant), JavaScript/TypeScript (Stryker),
# Flask (Python — mutmut), Go (go-gremlins).
```

behavioral-testing-standard.md gains a Tier-3 addendum noting the supported stacks and the bash scope-seal with the 411b epic ID reference. plugins/dso/docs/contracts/mutation-testing-findings.md notes the scope decision. plugins/dso/docs/CI-INTEGRATION.md updated to document mutation-testing parallel job semantics, per-stack timeout handling, ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT behavior, and TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation. Reviewer assertion: code-reviewer-test-quality (or equivalent test-quality reviewer agent) flags any proposed bash-mutation-tooling additions as a scope violation.

SC9 (synthetic end-to-end test): Ten scenarios covering happy paths, adversarial paths, and post-calibration end-to-end loop:
(a) Phase 1 — PR with Python file changes triggers mutmut; PR comment posted with calibration-mode kill-rate telemetry.
(b) Phase 2 — PR with Python + JS + Go file changes produces aggregate PR comment with per-stack stats.
(c) Phase 3 — fixture with 20-PR telemetry + 4-week elapsed AND no existing mutation-calibration-review story produces exactly one calibration-review story ticket with all required fields. Re-running the same fixture produces no duplicate.
(d) Phase 4 — fixture with mutation.calibration.completed=true + per-stack threshold + synthetic breach produces a bug ticket with all required fields including 4-field blurb (max 60 words) and content-hash dedup tag. Re-running the same fixture produces no duplicate bug.
(e) Phase 5 — dispatch consolidated /dso:onboarding against a Python-only fixture project: mutation.python.enabled=true; mutation-testing.yml present in .github/workflows/; tickets-branch push permission scope present.
(f) skip-mutation-testing PR label opts out: workflow runs but no mutation jobs execute; PR comment surfaces opt-out confirmation.
(g) mutants_generated=0 produces no bug ticket (PR touched only non-mutable code).
(h) runtime_exceeded partial result is emitted in findings JSON when per-stack timeout fires.
(i) ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT: all stacks return runtime_exceeded=true; PR comment surfaces warning; no bug ticket created even in threshold mode.
(j) Post-calibration end-to-end loop validation: PR with known-undertested function (mutant survives) against repo with mutation.calibration.completed=true AND per-stack threshold committed produces an auto-created bug ticket appearing in `ticket list --type=bug --status=open`. Same PR with added killing test produces no new bug ticket. Confirms the feedback loop is live end-to-end.

SC10 (validation signal): mutation-testing.yml referenced in CLAUDE.md Quick Reference table as the project's mutation-testing surface. mutation-testing-findings.md listed in plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ index. Both references link to 411b epic for context. Verify by: grep CLAUDE.md for "mutation-testing.yml" AND `ls plugins/dso/docs/contracts/` shows mutation-testing-findings.md.

## Approach

5 sequential phases with an explicit interim release gate:

- Phase 1: SC1 (contract) + SC2 (Python pilot CI workflow)
- Phase 2: SC3 (Ruby + JS/TS + Go expansion)

Phases 1-2 (Python pilot + polyglot expansion) constitute a shippable informational-mode increment; Phases 3-5 follow in the same milestone:

- Phase 3: SC4 (calibration auto-surfacing)
- Phase 4: SC5 (threshold-mode enforcement + auto-bug-creation)
- Phase 5: SC6 + SC7 (onboarding + create-dso-app.sh integration) + SC8 (scope-seal documentation)

SC9 + SC10 (synthetic + validation signal) verified across phases as each ships.

## Scenario Analysis (Blue Team surviving)

- Per-stack mutation runtime explosion on large PRs (critical/performance): partially mitigated by SC2 max_files_per_run auto-skip + SC3 per-stack timeout caps + ALL_STACKS_TIMEOUT handling; residual is the case where most-but-not-all stacks time out.
- CI compute cost budget at scale (critical/cost): partially mitigated by skip-mutation-testing PR label + concurrency group + per-stack runtime caps; no org-level monthly-minute budget guard; accepted as residual for first version.
- Tool version drift / pin yanking (important/reliability): partially mitigated by fallback_versions chain + TOOL_INSTALL_FAILED annotation; residual is the case where all fallback versions are also unavailable.
- Calibration thresholds become stale as codebase evolves (moderate/correctness): unmitigated; no automatic re-calibration trigger; accepted as residual — operator may flip mutation.calibration.completed=false manually to re-enter calibration mode.
- Calibration data poisoned by low-quality initial test suites (moderate/correctness): partially mitigated by SC4 self-reflection prompt; no automatic floor enforcement on observed median.
- Monorepo diff scoping failure in Python with shared package dependencies (moderate/correctness): unmitigated; documented limitation of incremental-mode mutmut on monorepos.
- Phase 5 blocked indefinitely if 136b-6758 slips (moderate/planning): unmitigated; no degraded-mode onboarding path specified; if 136b-6758 slips significantly, Phase 5 is rescoped at that time.

## Out of Scope

- Bash mutation testing — no mature ecosystem tool; SCOPE-SEALED with rationale documented in SC8.
- Promotion to merge-blocking gate — reserved for a future hybrid epic informed by calibration data; this epic ships warn-only / informational-only.
- Pre-commit mutation invocation — operationally untenable per the time-cost analysis (1–4 min added to every commit).
- Nightly batch runs — PR-time only in this version.
- Mutation testing within the llm-review job itself — separate parallel job per the architectural decision.
- Test-writer agent prompt modifications — 411b's feedback loop is indirect via auto-created bugs flowing through /dso:fix-bug and 69e8's negative-example graduation; 411b does not modify how tests are written.
- Project-side dependency-manifest modifications — no pyproject.toml / package.json / Gemfile / go.mod additions in host projects (CI-installs-on-demand).
- Org-level monthly-minute cost budget guard — not specified in first version; can be a follow-on if cost becomes a concern.
- Automatic threshold re-calibration trigger — not specified in first version; operator flips mutation.calibration.completed=false manually if recalibration is needed.

## Dependencies

HARD:
- 136b-6758-ba12-47fc (Consolidate project-setup skills into resume-aware /dso:onboarding) — required for SC6. Phase 5's onboarding integration consolidates onto the unified /dso:onboarding rather than fragmenting across /dso:onboarding + /dso:init separately. Phases 1-4 ship independently while 136b-6758 is implemented in parallel.

SOFT (coordination, not blocking):
- a03c-d55e — closure-checks-aware verifier consumes 411b's auto-created bugs.
- 94ed-f55c — surviving-mutant findings can optionally map back to intent_id via the manifest for downstream analysis; not required for the core gate.
- d566-afa6 — indirect downstream consumer via 69e8's negative-example graduation.
- 69e8-af39 — auto-created bugs are 69e8's input signal; 69e8 extracts negative-example patterns from these bugs.
- d765-a3b6-84bd-4816 — create-dso-app.sh rewrite coordination. If d765-a3b6 ships first, 411b's additions integrate on top of its rewrite; if 411b ships first, d765-a3b6's rewrite must preserve 411b's mutation-testing hooks. Coordination via ticket comment on d765-a3b6 at Phase 3 ticket integration.

## Planning Intelligence Log

- Web research (Step 2): not triggered. Sufficient context inherited from d566-afa6 brainstorm's three-stream research synthesis (Meta TestGen-LLM 2025, Stryker --incremental, mutmut, PIT scmMutationCoverage, mull, go-gremlins, OOPSLA 2025 PBT evidence).
- Scenario analysis (Step 3): triggered (SCs >= 5); 20 red-team scenarios surfaced; 13 mitigated-by-spec after blue-team filter; 7 surviving (most partial-mitigations on inherent runtime/cost residuals and moderate-severity items deferred).
- Cross-epic scan (Step 2.25): 1 conflict (136b-6758 hard dep, expected); 2 considerations (d765-a3b6 coordination, 69e8 consumer); 3 benign.
- Bot-psychologist (Step 5): triggered (LLM-instruction signal — modifies /dso:onboarding via 136b-6758 consolidation, create-dso-app.sh, and adds LLM-consumed bug-blurb content). Five risks folded: anti-sycophancy tradeoffs-first onboarding (SC6), single-stack auto-default (SC6), p25 anti-anchor reference table with explicit column headers (SC4), bash scope-seal block + reviewer assertion (SC8), 4-field structured auto-bug blurb max 60 words (SC5).
- Fidelity review (Step 4): Agent Clarity (5, 4), Scope (4, 4, 4, 4), Value (4, 4). All dimensions >= 4 after one revision cycle.
- Scale context (Step 0): small-to-medium per-PR; mutation runs scoped to diffed lines only.
- Session-signal override for complexity routing: success_criteria_count = 10 (>= 7 threshold) — would route to /dso:preplanning full mode if invoked; preplanning explicitly deferred this session.
- User-directed design decisions during brainstorm:
  - Polyglot first-class for Python, Ruby, JS/TS (including NextJS), Flask, Go; bash explicitly out of scope due to ecosystem-tool absence.
  - CI parallel with llm-review; not a required merge check.
  - Calibration-first delivery; thresholds set by human after telemetry-floor auto-surfaces a review ticket.
  - Threshold breach auto-creates a bug ticket with explanatory blurb context for the investigating agent.
  - CI-installs-on-demand (no project-side dependency-manifest changes; no local-env weight).
  - Onboarding-side integration consolidated onto 136b-6758's unified /dso:onboarding rather than fragmenting across init+onboarding separately.
  - dso setup script (create-dso-app.sh) updated for new-project scaffolding to include mutation-testing configuration.
